subject: Sherpa live ingest: intermittent parse corruption causing stalls

Subject: Live ingest stalls / parsing corruption seen in production

Hi Karthik —

We started seeing intermittent stalls and a jump in p99 latency across our live ingest on Friday night. The symptoms: connection remains open but no tokens stream for 5–30s then resumes; error rate for streamed requests spikes from ~0.2% to 4.7% under periods of bursty traffic. Attached are a trace and a zipped bundle of logs from our edge and the SDK.

We validated that upstream payloads look normal — headers show chunked frames from our proxy. When we switch to Redwood via a small proxy that disables connection coalescing, the problem goes away.

This is impacting our checkout flows; we have an open incident on our side (link below). Can you confirm if anything changed recently in the client SDK or runtime that might affect header reassembly or streaming parser behavior?

Thanks,
Olivia

Subject: Fwd: Live ingest stalls / parsing corruption seen in production

Marissa / Ben —

Forwarding Sherpa’s incident. They provided logs showing stalled streams with open connections and intermittent token gaps. Repro signal: disabling connection coalescing at their proxy removes the issue.

What I’ve seen so far: in our dechunker/streaming parser there’s a tight path that assumes headers and framing boundaries will never be coalesced across more than one read boundary. Under high-multiplexing and when upstream TCP coalesces frames, a race in the parser’s state machine can 1) merge two header blocks and 2) end up dropping a small portion of the trailer; the connection stays open but the token stream appears to stall until a keepalive or a subsequent frame unlocks the state.

Ben — can you validate reproduction on the SDK connector and confirm whether this is an SDK-side parser bug (meaning customers who upgrade the npm package will be fixed) or a server-side acceptance behavior? If it’s SDK-side we should prepare an immediate patch and a clear rollback for Sherpa.

If this hits production broadly we’ll need exec visibility. Evelyn — tagging you because Sherpa is a top 10 revenue customer for Dedicated; we should be ready with communications if this escalates.

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-22 12:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Live ingest stalls / parsing corruption seen in production

Quick update — I reproduced locally this morning using Sherpa’s traffic generator and a small proxy that simulates Nagle/coalescing behavior. Steps:
1) Old SDK connector v3.1.2: no reproductions.
2) SDK connector v3.2.0 (released two weeks ago): consistent stalls when we set the upstream to coalesce frames (every 3rd read boundary merges a header chunk + partial trailer).

Root cause: an off-by-one in the streaming parser’s buffer consumption path (connector/protocol/dechunker.cc) when headers span multiple reads. Under coalesced reads the parser assumes the header boundary marker appears only once and occasionally consumes past the CRLF sequence, leaving the trailer bytes in limbo. The runtime treats this as a partial message and waits for more data — which manifests as a stall.

Mitigation: I can push a hotfix branch to revert the buffer-change and add a defensive check to tolerate merged header blocks; patch will be small and we can publish a 3.2.1 SDK today. I also have a server-side extra validation we can back-deploy as a fallback to close the state machine if we see stalled token progress for >5s.

Recommended immediate actions:
- Hotfix 3.2.1 to npm and a patch to the hosted runtime acceptance layer.
- Ask Sherpa to temporarily pin to 3.1.2 if they can accept a client rollback while we ship the patch.
- Prepare a customer note and an incident postmortem timeline.

I’ll open the PR and start a CI run.
—Ben
Senior Software Engineer, Inference SDK

Impact: Sherpa is a top Dedicated customer; they’re in active incident and are asking for a timeline and mitigation. Ben can ship a 3.2.1 hotfix to the SDK today and we can also deploy a runtime guard to close stalled state machines as a fallback.
